question: When lead nitrate is mixed with potassium iodine, the precipitate formed is _______.
solution:
The correct answer is **__yellow color lead iodide__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The reaction between lead nitrate and potassium iodide is a type of **precipitation** and **double displacement reaction**.
 
• The lead nitrate [Pb(NO₃)₂] reacts with potassium iodide (Kl) causing exchange of ions between the reactants leading to the formation of **potassium nitrate (KNO₃) and a yellow precipitate of lead iodide (PbI₂).**
 
• The potassium of the potassium iodide **replaces** the lead of the lead nitrate in this reaction.
 
• The reaction involved is given below: 
 
 
• **Pb(NO****₃)₂ (aq) + 2KI (aq) → PbI₂ (s) + 2KNO₃ (aq)​**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Lead iodide is **colorless** when in aqueous solution but when precipitated, it is yellow in color. 
 
• Lead iodide is precipitated because it is** insoluble in water.**
 
• The color of the lead iodide solution is colorless because the reactants that are **lead nitrate and potassium iodide **are also colorless in aqueous solution.
